topics.title: AI-assisted math claim draws scrutiny
topics.summary: An Anthropic employee says work with Claude helped produce a proof of the Riemann Hypothesis. Mathematicians say the claim will need careful independent review before it can be accepted.
topics.discussionPrompt: If an AI helped solve a famously difficult puzzle, would you celebrate the tool, the person guiding it, or the whole strange collaboration?

topics.title: Florida rains move northward
topics.summary: After historic flooding in parts of Florida, heavy rains are shifting farther north. The changing weather pattern is keeping residents and forecasters alert.
topics.discussionPrompt: When a stormy week changes your plans, are you a cozy-indoor-person, a weather-app checker, or someone who still insists the outing can happen?

topics.title: COP31 talks continue past deadline
topics.summary: Climate negotiations in Antalya continued beyond their scheduled end as countries sought agreement on the final text, including language on fossil fuels and climate finance.
topics.discussionPrompt: In a huge group project with one last sticking point, do you push for perfect wording, accept a compromise, or volunteer to make the coffee run?

topics.title: Nvidia export rules remain unchanged
topics.summary: The U.S. Treasury secretary said additional restrictions were not needed for Nvidia chip exports to China, keeping attention on how technology trade rules may evolve.
topics.discussionPrompt: What makes a piece of tech feel more exciting to you: speed, clever design, a useful everyday feature, or the story behind how it was made?

topics.title: Mosquito study offers dengue hope
topics.summary: Researchers reported strong evidence that mosquitoes bred with Wolbachia bacteria can help reduce the spread of dengue and chikungunya, offering a promising public-health tool.
topics.discussionPrompt: If a tiny creature could help solve a big human problem, would that make you see it differently—or would mosquitoes remain permanently unpopular?

topics.title: Wildlife bridge nears opening in Los Angeles
topics.summary: The world’s largest wildlife crossing is set to open above a Los Angeles-area freeway, creating a safer route for animals moving between habitats.
topics.discussionPrompt: If your neighborhood built a crossing just for animals, which creature would you hope to spot using it first?

topics.title: Ancient Roman library reopens
topics.summary: Rome’s restored Ulpia Library, a long-buried imperial-era site, is reopening to visitors after conservation work brought its history back into public view.
topics.discussionPrompt: If you could borrow one book from an ancient library, would you choose a lost comedy, a travel journal, a recipe book, or something else?

topics.title: France preserves home movies
topics.summary: Archivists and activists in France are rescuing aging home movies, preserving everyday memories and giving old film a new life for future viewers.
topics.discussionPrompt: What ordinary moment from your life would become surprisingly interesting footage fifty years from now?

topics.title: Greenland’s food scene gains attention
topics.summary: Greenland’s growing culinary scene is putting Arctic ingredients and local cooking traditions in the spotlight, drawing visitors interested in food shaped by place.
topics.discussionPrompt: If you could try a meal that captures one landscape, would you pick Arctic coast, rainforest, desert, mountains, or somewhere closer to home?

topics.title: Girl Scout cookies inspire a history look
topics.summary: A new look at Girl Scout cookies traces how the familiar fundraiser became a lasting symbol of entrepreneurship, community work, and a very recognizable seasonal tradition.
topics.discussionPrompt: What annual tradition instantly tells you a new season has arrived: a certain food, a holiday display, a smell in the air, or a favorite show?
